title: Spiced molasses cookies
subtitle: dark, crinkle-topped biscuits with a sticky, fudgy centre and strong spicing
excerpt: Spiced molasses cookies are dark, strongly spiced biscuits with a crinkled top, crisp edges, and a sticky, fudgy centre when freshly baked. Molasses gives a deep, slightly bitter note and the characteristic dark colour. The dough is chilled before baking so the cookies hold a thick shape and crinkle rather than spread flat. They are best the day of baking.
sourceNotes: Molasses cookies are a classic American spice biscuit documented in American cookbooks from the nineteenth century onward. The crinkle-top appearance comes from rolling in sugar before baking, a technique documented in mid-twentieth century American baking manuals.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked cookies in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best the day of baking. Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 3 days.

content.text: Spiced molasses cookies are dark, chewy biscuits made with molasses, ground ginger, and warm spices. They are rolled in sugar before baking, which gives the characteristic crinkled surface and a thin sugary crust around the fudgy centre. Chill the dough for at least an hour before baking; the cold dough crinkles as it bakes rather than spreading flat.

Whisk together the flour, bicarbonate of soda, and spices in a bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk together the oil, brown sugar, molasses, and egg until combined. Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until a dough forms.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour, until the dough is firm enough to roll into balls without sticking.
Heat the oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Line two baking trays with baking paper. Put the caster sugar in a shallow bowl.
Scoop heaped teaspoons of dough and roll into balls between your palms. Roll each ball in the caster sugar to coat all over, then place on the prepared trays with at least 5 cm between each one.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the tops are crinkled and the edges are set. The centres will look underdone; they firm up as they cool. Leave on the tray for 10 minutes before moving.

attrs.problem: Cookies spreading flat with no crinkle
attrs.avoid: Avoid warm or unchilled dough; it spreads too quickly in the oven before the surface has time to set and crinkle.
attrs.fix: Chill the dough for at least 1 hour. If you can, chill it overnight for even more pronounced crinkles.

attrs.problem: Hard and crisp all the way through rather than fudgy in the centre
attrs.avoid: Avoid overbaking; molasses cookies set quickly once the centre is done.
attrs.fix: Remove when the edges look set but the centre looks underdone. The centres should look almost raw. They will firm to a fudgy texture as they cool.
